prompts.text: We have fifteen minutes to make a short film using only what's in the room. Who becomes the director?
Which friend would take a casual karaoke performance as seriously as a stadium concert?
Making hilariously bad portraits of each other or writing a two-minute radio drama?
The most entertaining group projects usually begin with someone saying, 'This will be easy.'
When everyone contributes to a playlist, the transitions reveal how little the group agrees about music.
Tell me about a harmless creative challenge that became much funnier than planned.
If we had to design matching T-shirts, what's the one phrase we'd never agree to put on them?
Our group becomes a band for one performance. Who gets the microphone, and who's better kept away from it?
Inventing a silly dance together or creating a fake advert for an everyday household item?
Somebody who brings their own costume to a casual themed gathering deserves the main character role.
Who's most likely to claim they don't care about winning and then request an immediate rematch?
We play a game where you lose a point every time you say 'literally'. Who is out first?
A competitive quiz about each other's habits or a contest guessing the price of random groceries?
You can tell when a friend is losing a board game by how suddenly they start criticising the rules.
The group should appoint an independent referee before starting any game of charades.
Tell me about a game that had everyone laughing too hard to finish.
Which harmless talent would you put forward if we had to represent our group in a competition?
There's one final biscuit and the group decides it must be won through a trivia question. Who writes the question?
A silly obstacle course or a timed challenge to wrap the neatest birthday present?
A friend who loses graciously makes any game better, but a dramatic loser gives us stories for years.
What's the funniest reason our group has ever changed its plans at the last minute?
We're all dressed up for an event and discover it's next weekend. What do we do with the evening?
An unexpected stop at a roadside attraction or stumbling into a local festival nobody knew about?
The best stories from a group outing rarely feature the part everyone carefully scheduled.
A plan labelled 'quick errand' has a way of becoming a three-hour adventure with friends.
Tell me about a time the backup plan became everyone's favourite part of the day.
Which of our friends is most likely to turn a missed train into an opportunity for snacks?
Half the group brings umbrellas and half arrives in sunglasses. Who gets to comment on the forecast?
Trying a new place because the first was closed or moving the hangout into someone's kitchen?
A cancelled outing is not truly cancelled until the group chat has discussed at least five alternatives.
If our friends secretly planned a surprise for us, who would accidentally reveal it first?
We have to plan a birthday surprise while the birthday person is sitting at the next table. Who makes it obvious?
A scavenger hunt with ridiculous clues or a surprise picnic where everyone contributes one item?
The friend who keeps asking suspiciously specific questions is rarely good at hiding a surprise.
A harmless practical joke stops being funny the moment somebody genuinely feels embarrassed.
Tell me about a surprise that fell apart but somehow became a better memory.
Which friend would be the worst person to trust with keeping an amusing secret for twenty-four hours?
Everyone is told to bring something blue to a gathering without knowing why. Who asks the most questions?
Inventing a silly fake award ceremony or putting together a heartfelt video with mildly embarrassing clips?
The real skill in planning a surprise is keeping everyone informed without sending a message to the wrong chat.
If our group opened a tiny café, who would insist on inventing the most complicated signature drink?
We have to pitch a completely ridiculous product idea to strangers in sixty seconds. Who does the presentation?
Our imaginary business selling novelty socks or our imaginary service finding lost remote controls?
The first disagreement in a group business would be over the name, not the money.
Tell me about a silly money-making scheme you and a friend invented as children.
The friend with the neatest handwriting is always volunteered to make the sign.
Which of us would become the unofficial customer-service manager after two minutes?
We have to open a stall at a weekend market with things already in our homes. What could we sell?
Running a bookshop with cats or a cinema that shows only cult classics?
Some of the wildest group ideas deserve one imaginary business meeting and absolutely no investors.
